questions.q: Why does bronze ingestion deliberately skip inferSchema and type casting?
options: Bronze wants the data exactly as it arrived — any cleaning or casting belongs to silver, not bronze
inferSchema doesn't work with Delta tables
It's a bug that should eventually be fixed
Bronze tables can only ever hold string columns
questions.explain: This is a deliberate design choice, not an oversight — cleaning happens one layer later, in silver.

questions.q: What do metadata columns like _ingested_at and _source_file track?
options: When and from where each row arrived — bookkeeping that doesn't exist in the original source data
The final business value each row represents
The Unity Catalog permissions granted on the row
The exact PySpark version used to process the row
questions.explain: These let anyone later ask which ingestion run produced a given row, without guessing.

questions.q: Why does bronze keep rows that look obviously malformed or wrong?
options: So that if silver's cleaning logic has a bug discovered later, bronze still has the original, unmodified row to reprocess from
Because Delta tables cannot filter rows at all
Because filtering rows would violate ACID transactions
Bronze rows are automatically fixed by Delta before being stored
questions.explain: Filtering too early means that row is gone for good, with no way back to reprocess it.

questions.q: What write mode does bronze normally use, and why?
options: mode("append") — every new batch adds more rows, making bronze a genuine, permanent record rather than a replaced snapshot
mode("overwrite") — each new batch replaces everything that came before
Bronze tables cannot be written to more than once
mode("merge") — every batch updates existing rows in place
questions.explain: This is the same append mode from Foundations Lesson 60 and this course's Lesson 16.

questions.q: What's the one genuinely new thing in bronze ingestion compared to a plain Foundations-style CSV read?
options: saveAsTable(), writing straight into a real, persistent, named Delta table
Using Python for the first time
Reading a CSV file at all
Applying a schema with StructType
questions.explain: This is Lesson 16's saveAsTable() pattern, now applied to the very first stage of a real pipeline.
